# **PREAMBLE**  {#preamble}

We, the students of the Indian Institute of Technology Madras BS Degree Programme, give ourselves a Constitution to promote, through a democratic representative system, the common welfare of all students by:

1. responding to and resolving student concerns,  
2. representing students to the administration,  
3. sharing institute resources,  
4. promoting liberty, equality and fraternity,  
5. promoting unity in diversity,  
6. providing opportunities for all-round excellence, and  
7. promoting cooperation among the members of the campus community. 

For these ends, we are resolved to respect and abide by this Constitution, to reflect maturity in our thoughts and actions, and to cultivate an atmosphere of mutual respect, trust, and harmony. 

# **CHAPTER I \- STUDENT EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE** {#chapter-i---student-executive-committee}

## **SECTION I – INTRODUCTION** {#section-i-–-introduction}

The Student Executive Committee (SEC) is constituted to support the Student Affairs team in maintaining the student community infrastructure and coordinating the activities of the Upper House Council, Lower House Council, student societies, and the Paradox team. The committee facilitates the implementation of student initiatives and promotes effective engagement across the student community.

## **SECTION II – INTERPRETATION** {#section-ii-–-interpretation}

1. **“SEC”** means the Student Executive Committee constituted by this instrument.  
2. **“Programme”** refers to the IIT Madras Bachelor of Science degree.  
3. **“Student Affairs”** includes the Head of Student Affairs or duly authorised delegate.  
4. **“SAF”** denotes the Student Activities Fund.  
5. **“CGPA”** signifies the cumulative grade-point average recorded at the close of the most recent term.  
6. **“Council Year”** denotes 3 consecutive academic terms, starting from July 1st.  
7. **“Simple majority”** denotes more than half of those present and voting.  
8. Other terms bear the meanings assigned in the Constitutions of Houses and Societies.  
9. The Head of Student Affairs derives authority from the BS Program Coordinators, whose decisions shall be final and binding in cases of ambiguity or interpretation.

## **SECTION III – ESTABLISHMENT AND COMPOSITION** {#section-iii-–-establishment-and-composition}

1. The SEC is hereby constituted to support the Student Affairs team in coordinating and facilitating student activities across the Programme.  
2. The Committee shall comprise seven (7) voting secretaries & four (4) voting Programme Representatives as follows :  
   

|  | Secretary | Designation | Minimum CGPA |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Student Relations Secretary | SRS | ≥ 7.5 |
| 2 | Finance Secretary | FS | ≥ 7.5 |
| 3 | Sports Secretary | SpS | ≥ 7.5 |
| 4 | Technical Secretary | TS | ≥ 7.5 |
| 5 | Cultural Secretary | CS | ≥ 7.5 |
| 6 | Election & Ethics Secretary | EES | ≥ 7.5 |
| 7 | Web Operations & Multimedia Secretary | WOMS | ≥ 7.5 |
| 8 | Data Science & Applications Programme Representative | DS Rep | ≥ 8 |
| 9 | Electronic Systems Programme Representative | ES Rep | ≥ 8 |
| 10 | Aeronautics & Space Technology Programme Representative | AE Rep | ≥ 8 |
| 11 | Management & Data Science Programme Representative | MG Rep | ≥ 8 |

3. Student Affairs shall attend with a veto vote.

## **SECTION IV – ELIGIBILITY & TENURE** {#section-iv-–-eligibility-&-tenure}

1. To be eligible for appointment to any position in the SEC, a student must:  
   1. be on the rolls of the Programme at the time of appointment;  
   2. possess a CGPA not less than 7.5 (except where a higher CGPA is stipulated);  
   3. have no active Registration-Keep-Alive status;  
   4. have no conviction for academic or non-academic misconduct.  
2. Appointments to the SEC shall be made online during the final fortnight of December, under the supervision of Student Affairs.  
3. The term of  the SEC members shall be determined in accordance with the directives and discretion of Student Affairs.

## **SECTION V – POWERS & RESPONSIBILITIES OF SECRETARIES & REPRESENTATIVES** {#section-v-–-powers-&-responsibilities-of-secretaries-&-representatives}

1. **Student Relations Secretary (SRS)**  
   1. Provide support for operational queries (meeting recording, streaming etc.);  
   2. Manage all official communication channels and social-media handles of Student Activities;  
   3. Issue timely bulletins, newsletters and ensure responsive engagement;  
   4. Manage Student Activity Calendar and Student Activity Announcements Google Group.  
2. **Finance Secretary (FS)**  
   1. Convene the Finance Committee constituted by Student Affairs, with the following members::  
      1. Finance Secretary (Major role for SAF event, Member for Paradox Proposal Selection)  
      2. Paradox Finance Core/Deputy Core (Major role in Paradox Proposal Selection, Member for other SAF events)  
      3. Paradox Secretary handling Finance, Facilities & Requirements  
      4. Faculty Mentor(s)  
   2. Process SAF applications from Event Secretaries and maintain appropriate ledgers;  
   3. Review MOUs and sponsorship agreements initiated by student bodies;  
   4. Serve as point of contact with the STACT Office and BS Accounts team;  
   5. Review event and meetup budgets for approval by Student Affairs;  
   6. Review and assist with event/meetup reimbursement formalities;  
   7. Manage SAF workflows.  
3. **Sports Secretary (SpS)**  
   1. Convene the Sports Committee constituted by Student Affairs, with the following members:  
      1. Sports Secretary (Major role for SAF event, Member for Paradox Proposal Selection)  
      2. Paradox Sports Core/Deputy Core (Major role in Paradox Proposal Selection, Member for other SAF events)  
      3. Faculty Mentor(s)  
   2. Route sports proposals seeking SAF through the Committee;  
   3. Promote and oversee sports activities within the Programme;  
   4. Act as the Event Department Committee, fulfilling responsibilities outlined in Societies constitution;  
   5. Identify and cultivate students as a common talent pool.  
4. **Technical Secretary (TS)**  
   1. Convene the Technicals Committee constituted by Student Affairs, with the following members::  
      1. Technicals Secretary (Major role for SAF event, Member for Paradox Proposal Selection)  
      2. Paradox Technicals Core/Deputy Core (Major role in Paradox Proposal Selection, Member for other SAF events)  
      3. Faculty Mentor(s)  
   2. Route technical proposals seeking SAF through the Committee;  
   3. Promote and oversee technical activities within the Programme;  
   4. Act as the Event Department Committee, fulfilling responsibilities outlined in Societies constitution;  
   5. Identify and cultivate students as a common talent pool.  
5. **Cultural Secretary (CS)**  
   1. Convene the Cultural Committee constituted by Student Affairs, with the following members::  
      1. Cultural Secretary (Major role for SAF event, Member for Paradox Proposal Selection)  
      2. Paradox Cultural Core (Major role in Paradox Proposal Selection, Member for other SAF events)  
      3. Faculty Mentor(s)  
   2. Route cultural proposals seeking SAF through the Committee;  
   3. Promote and oversee cultural activities within the Programme;  
   4. Act as the Event Department Committee, fulfilling responsibilities outlined in Societies constitution;  
   5. Identify and cultivate students as a common talent pool.  
6. **Election & Ethics Secretary (EES)**  
   1. Coordinate with the Student Election Commission and Grievance Redressal Committee;  
   2. Facilitate the conducting of General Student Body Elections;  
   3. Maintain and create awareness about the Students’ Code of Conduct and Student Interaction Guidelines;  
   4. Act as liaison with the IITM CCASH and Wellness Centre under the supervision of Student Affairs.  
7. **Web Operations & Multimedia Secretary (WOMS)**  
   1. Maintain the Programme’s official student website (\<iitmbs.org\>) and election portal;  
   2. Develop and maintain a unified student portal consolidating services and announcements;  
   3. Create and facilitate the publishing of multimedia content.

## **SECTION VI – COMMITTEE PROCEDURE** {#section-vi-–-committee-procedure}

1. The SEC shall meet at least once every calendar month.  
2. Extraordinary meetings may be convened by at least 6 SEC members or by Student Affairs.  
3. Quorum shall be five (6) voting SEC members.  
4. Decisions are by simple majority; in the event of a tie, Student Affairs shall cast a deciding vote.  
5. Minutes of Meeting (MoM) shall be circulated to all students holding Positions of Responsibility and Student Affairs within seven (7) days.  
6. An annual SEC report, including audited SAF utilisation, shall be published within thirty (30) days of the Committee Year’s end.

## **SECTION VII – CONDUCT, REMOVAL & SUCCESSION** {#section-vii-–-conduct,-removal-&-succession}

1. All SEC members shall exemplify integrity, inclusivity and adherence to Institute regulations.  
2. Grounds for removal include misconduct, dereliction, academic ineligibility, or breach of conduct standards.  
3. Removal procedure shall be based on a decision by Student Affairs.  
4. Upon removal or resignation, a new appointment shall be made by Student Affairs.

## **SECTION VIII – FINANCE** {#section-viii-–-finance}

1. The SAF shall be administered by the Finance Secretary in accordance with Institute financial rules.  
2. Disbursements require:  
   1.  written proposal endorsed by the relevant Domain Committee;  
   2. majority approval of the SEC;  
   3. countersignature of Student Affairs where mandated.

## **SECTION IX – AMENDMENT, GOVERNING AUTHORITY & COMMENCEMENT** {#section-ix-–-amendment,-governing-authority-&-commencement}

1. This chapter may be amended by a two-thirds (⅔) vote of the full SEC and approval of Student Affairs.  
2. No amendment shall contravene Institute statutes or policy.  
3. Directives of IIT Madras BS Student Affairs supersede any conflicting clause or decision herein.

# **CHAPTER II \- HOUSES** {#chapter-ii---houses}

## **SECTION I – INTRODUCTION** {#section-i-–-introduction-1}

The Houses are twelve student bodies named after Indian forests in order to foster community, advance scholarship, safeguard welfare, and ensure orderly self-government.

## **SECTION II – GENERAL PROVISIONS** {#section-ii-–-general-provisions}

1. Definitions  
   1. House denotes one of the twelve student bodies named after Indian forests, defined under this constitution.  
   2. The programme signifies the IITM BS academic programme.  
   3. Student Affairs includes the Head of Student Affairs or duly authorised delegate.  
   4. SEC denotes the Student Executive Committee of the Programme.  
   5. Position of Responsibility (PoR) means any position enumerated in Annex A to this Constitution.  
   6. Academic Year signifies the period of 3 consecutive academic terms, starting from July 1st unless redefined by the Institute.

## **SECTION III – HOUSES AND MEMBERSHIP** {#section-iii-–-houses-and-membership}

1. Establishment of Houses  
   1. The Programme shall comprise twelve (12) Houses: Bandipur, Corbett, Gir, Kanha, Kaziranga, Nallamala, Namdapha, Nilgiri, Pichavaram, Saranda, Sundarbans, and Wayanad.  
2. Regions  
   1. For administrative purposes each House shall recognise ten (10) Regions listed in Schedule I hereto.  
3. Membership  
   1. Every student on the rolls of the Programme is ipso facto a Member of one House and one Region.  
   2. Membership is automatic and shall not depend upon geographical domicile but exam city centre selected during registration.  
4. Rights and Duties of Members  
   1. Rights:  
      1. to vote,  
      2. to stand for election subject to eligibility, and  
      3. to participate in House activities.  
   2. Duties :  
      1. to uphold a discrimination-free environment,  
      2. academic integrity,  
      3. intellectual property rights,  
      4. privacy, and personal accountability.  
      5. all roles and responsibilities remain binding as per the student hand book

   

## **SECTION IV – GOVERNANCE ORGANS** {#section-iv-–-governance-organs}

1. Upper House Council (UHC)  
   1. Constitution and Status  
      1. Each House shall constitute a House Council which shall be the supreme representative and administrative organ of the House, subject to Student Affairs oversight.  
      2. The Upper House Council shall consist of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary from each of the 12 houses, each possessing one (1) vote.  
   2. Eligibility  
      1. A candidate for Secretary or Deputy Secretary must :   
         1) be not more than twenty-five (25) years of age on Nomination Day;    
         2) possess a CGPA not less than 7.5 and be free of Registration-Keep-Alive status;    
         3) have completed a minimum of thirty-two (32) academic credits;    
         4) have held a PoR for three (3) consecutive terms;    
         5) have no record of academic or non-academic misconduct;    
         6) not have previously served as House Secretary;    
         7) not have previously served as the House Deputy Secretary if standing again for the post of Deputy Secretary;    
         8) intend to remain on the rolls for three (3) consecutive terms post-election.    
         9) Student Affairs holds the power to waive any criteria in exceptional cases.

   3. Election and Tenure  
      1. Elections shall be conducted online in the final fortnight of June under the supervision of Student Affairs.  
      2. The electorate shall be all Members of the House.  
      3. The term of PoR shall be one (1) Academic Year.  
   4. Powers and Responsibilities  
      1. House Secretaries/Deputy Secretaries shall :  
         1) determine House policy and strategic direction;  
         2) hold the right to appoint and dismiss the Web Administrator;  
         3) approve budgets and annual calendars for their houses;  
         4) convene House Council meetings at least once every fourteen (14) days;  
         5) organise not fewer than ten (10) House meet-ups and two (2) academic-support events per Academic Year;  
         6) ensure maintenance of their respective house official digital platforms;  
         7) submit a termly House Report to Student Affairs;  
         8) adjudicate grievances escalated from the LHC.  
2. Lower House Council (LHC)  
   1. Constitution  
      1. The LHC shall comprise ten (10) Regional Coordinators (RCs), one elected from each Region per House.  
      2. The Secretary and Deputy Secretary shall sit ex officio without vote.  
   2. Eligibility of Regional Coordinators  
      1. An RC candidate must :  
         1) be not more than twenty-five (25) years of age on Nomination Day;  
         2) possess a CGPA not less than 7.5 and be free of RKA;  
         3) have completed at least fifty per-cent (50%) of the curriculum then available and at least one (1) academic term;  
         4) have no disciplinary violation record;  
         5) intend to remain on the rolls for three (3) consecutive terms post-election.  
      2. Election and Tenure  
         1) RCs shall be elected annually, concurrently with UHC elections, by Members of the relevant Region in the house.  
         2) The Election Commission shall administer the poll.  
         3) The term of PoR shall be one (1) Academic Year.  
   3. Functions of the LHC  
      1. The LHC shall :  
         1) facilitate two-way communication between Members and the UHC;  
         2) disseminate programme notices and ensure compliance with deadlines;  
         3) organise at least one (1) online meet per month and one (1) offline meet-up per tenure in each Region;  
         4) conduct one (1) Orientation and one (1) Feedback session per term;  
         5) arrange mentoring and academic support;  
         6) submit monthly Minutes of Meeting and a term-end Regional Report;  
         7) devote approximately two (2) hours weekly to tasks assigned by Student Affairs.  
3. Web Administrator  
   1. Appointment and Duties  
      1. The Secretary/Deputy Secretary of a house shall appoint one (1) Web Administrator for a term of one (1) year for their house.  
      2. The appointee shall be in good academic standing and free of disciplinary sanction.  
      3. The Web Administrator shall maintain House websites, mailing lists, Google Spaces, common email IDs, and digital archives.

## **SECTION V – ELECTORAL AND VACANCY PROVISIONS** {#section-v-–-electoral-and-vacancy-provisions}

1. General Rules  
   1. No candidate may contest more than one (1) PoR in the same election cycle.  
   2. Vacancies shall be filled within thirty (30) days by by-election or interim nomination approved by Student Affairs.  
   3. All electoral disputes shall be resolved by the Election Commission under Student Affairs.

## **SECTION VI – CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE** {#section-vi-–-conduct-and-discipline}

1. Code of Conduct  
   Members and PoRs shall observe the standards set forth in Section III, point 4 and such additional regulations as Student Affairs may promulgate.  
2. Removal from Position  
   1. A PoR may be removed for academic ineligibility, misconduct, or dereliction of duty.  
   2. Removal requires a simple majority of the relevant Council after ratification by Student Affairs.  
3. Impeachment  
   1. An impeachment proceeding against any elected UHC member can be initiated by one-fourth of the total strength of the electorate for a particular post. The impeachment motion must be initiated by writing an email to Student Affairs.  
   2. The representative shall be considered impeached if at least two-third of the electorate votes in the impeachment motion, and at least half of the votes support impeachment.  
   3. In case of any ambiguities regarding the impeachment rules the decision of Student Affairs shall remain final and binding.  
4. Grievance Redressal  
   The escalation sequence shall be: Member → RC → Secretary / Deputy Secretary → Student Affairs.

## **SECTION VII – COMMUNICATION, BRANDING, AND FINANCE** {#section-vii-–-communication,-branding,-and-finance}

1. Official Channels  
   1. All House communications shall employ their POR email IDs, the House Google Group, and Google Space.  
   2. A Google Space shall exist for the UHC, the LHC, and joint House deliberations, with Student Affairs.  
2. Use of Institute Name and Logo  
   No House shall use the name “IIT Madras” or any Institute emblem without prior written consent from the IITM BS Degree Team.  
3. Commercial Activity  
   Houses shall not undertake commercial ventures except with explicit Institute approval.

## 

## **SECTION VIII – AMENDMENT AND SUPREMACY** {#section-viii-–-amendment-and-supremacy}

1. Amendment  
   1. This chapter may be amended by a two-thirds (⅔) vote of both the UHC and the LHC, followed by ratification by Student Affairs.  
   2. Student Affairs retains the authority to override any provision herein.  
2. Supremacy  
   Where any clause of this Constitution conflicts with Institute statutes or directives, the latter shall prevail.

## **ANNEX A – RECOGNISED POSITIONS OF RESPONSIBILITY (PoRs)** {#annex-a-–-recognised-positions-of-responsibility-(pors)}

* Secretary (House);  
* Deputy Secretary (House);  
* Web Administrator;  
* Regional Coordinator / Group Leader;  
* Society Secretary, Deputy Secretary, or Coordinator;  
* Paradox Secretary;  
* Paradox Core, Deputy Core, or Super-Coordinator.  
* Secretary (SEC)

## **SCHEDULE I – RECOGNISED REGIONS** {#schedule-i-–-recognised-regions}

* Delhi (NCR);  
* Chennai;  
* Bengaluru;  
* Hyderabad;  
* Mumbai;  
* Kolkata;  
* Patna;  
* Chandigarh;  
* Lucknow;  
* International.

# **CHAPTER III \- SOCIETIES** {#chapter-iii---societies}

## **SECTION I – INTRODUCTION** {#section-i-–-introduction-2}

A Society is a group of students who work collaboratively to achieve a shared goal. They have a broad domain of industrial, academic, artistic, sports or socially inclined humanitarian causes, aiming to foster the holistic development of their members. Additionally, they provide support to the wider student community through awareness programs and relevant events in their respective domains. 

## **SECTION II – INTERPRETATION** {#section-ii-–-interpretation-1}

1. For the purposes of this Constitution :  
   1. “Society” is a group of students who work collaboratively to achieve a shared goal formed under the Societies Chapter.  
   2. “Domain” denotes one of three thematic clusters : Technical, Sports, Cultural.  
   3. “Department Secretary” is the SEC secretary appointed to supervise Societies within a Domain.  
   4. “Core Committee” (“CC”) is the governing body of a Society constituted under the Societies Chapter.  
   5. “General Body” (“GB”) comprises all Active Members of a Society.  
   6. “Active Member” is a student who has filled the membership renewal form in the past term.  
   7. “Interest Group” is a provisional pan-Programme body recognised under the Societies Chapter..  
   8. “Position of Responsibility” (“PoR”) is any recognized position listed in Annex A.  
   9. “Academic Year” signifies the period of 3 consecutive academic terms, starting from July 1st unless redefined by the Institute.  
   10. “Student Affairs” includes the Head of Student Affairs (HoSA) and any duly authorised delegate.  
   11. “SEC” denotes the Student Executive Council of the Programme.

## **SECTION III – INTEREST GROUPS** {#section-iii-–-interest-groups}

1. Nature and Purpose  
   1. An Interest Group is a provisional, pan-Programme initiative that explores a distinct area of expertise not currently covered by any existing Society. It holds the potential to evolve into a full-fledged Society based on its engagement and impact.  
2. Establishment  
   1. A student applicant shall e-mail a proposal to the relevant Event Department Secretary.  
   2. Upon approval the Interest Group is recognised for one (1) academic term.  
   3. The Interest Group will be incubated under the appropriate event department or under a society, at the society’s discretion. The decision will be up to the event department committee.  
   4. Academic/Non-Academic background of students shall be checked before they are allowed to open interest groups.  
3. Term and Extension  
   1. Recognition lasts one term; extension for a further term requires a satisfactory activity report endorsed by the Event Department Committee.  
   2. No Interest Group may exceed three (3) terms.  
4. Conversion to Society  
   1. After three active terms and verified execution of events at the Programme’s fests (Saavan, Margazhi and Paradox), an Interest Group may petition the Event Department Committee for Society status, subject to the committee’s discretion.  
5. Inactivity and Dismantling  
   1. Failure to meet activity standards renders an Interest Group inactive; credentials (G-Space or Social Handles) revert to the Event Department Committee.  
   2. The domain may thereafter be reassigned to new applicants in the future.

## **SECTION IV – RECOGNITION OF SOCIETIES** {#section-iv-–-recognition-of-societies}

1. Expression of Interest  
   1. Any “Interest Group” may seek recognition by submitting an Expression of Interest (“EoI”) to Event Department Committee containing :  
      1. proposed name and domain;  
      2. goals and intended activities;  
      3. record of prior activity (if evolved as an “Interest Group”);  
      4. action plan for each term of the Academic Year;  
      5. list of supporting students;  
      6. draft CC structure with roles and responsibilities;  
      7. proposed meeting frequency and quorum for CC and GB.  
   2. Upon approval, the Domain Committee shall facilitate an official e-mail ID for the Society.  
2. Disclaimer of Endorsement  
   1. Recognition shall not imply endorsement by IIT Madras BS; the Core Committee bears sole responsibility for the content and conduct of Society activities.

## **SECTION V – MEMBERSHIP** {#section-v-–-membership}

1. Eligibility and Admission  
   1. Every student on the rolls of the Programme may apply for membership in any Society.  
   2. Membership procedures shall be non-discriminatory and transparent.  
2. Term of Membership  
   1. Membership is valid for one (1) Academic Year and is renewable upon application.

## **SECTION VI – GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE** {#section-vi-–-governance-structure}

1. Organs of a Society  
   1. General Body (GB) – the sovereign body of Active Members;  
   2. Core Committee (CC) – elected or appointed members.  
2. One-Student-One-Position Rule  
   1. No student may hold more than one executive position of responsibility simultaneously across all Houses and Societies.  
3. Honor Code  
   1. Each Society shall incorporate the Institute’s non-discrimination policy, Code of Conduct and Honour Code into its bye-laws.

## **SECTION VII – CORE COMMITTEE AND POSITIONS OF RESPONSIBILITY** {#section-vii-–-core-committee-and-positions-of-responsibility}

1. Mandatory Positions  
   1. Every Society shall have, at minimum :  
      1. one Secretary;  
      2. one Deputy Secretary;  
      3. not more than two Co-ordinators.  
         Additional positions may be created with SEC/Student Affairs approval.  
2. Term of PoR  
   1. All positions of responsibility are held for one (1) Academic Year commencing 1 July.  
3. Duties  
   1. Secretary – overall leadership; convenes meetings; principal signatory; ensures compliance with reporting.  
   2. Deputy Secretary – assists the Secretary; acts in the Secretary’s absence; oversees operational teams.  
   3. Co-ordinators – execute specific projects and events as assigned by the Core Committee.  
4. Positional Rights and Definition  
   1. Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Coordinators (Core Committee) monitor the overall conduct and decision-making of the entity, ensuring it operates within the rights granted under this Constitution.  
   2. The core committee structure has three key positions in hierarchical order: Secretary (highest), Deputy Secretary, Coordinators. The immediate superior assumes rights and duties in the absence of a superior, ensuring continuity.  
   3. These positions are filled through internal elections/appointments among entity members. One tenure equals three academic terms, after which elections/appointments are held anew.  
   4. Secretaries and Deputy Secretaries are restricted to one elected or non-elected position in any student organization during their one-year or three-term tenure.  
   5. Secretaries/Deputy Secretaries can be impeached upon entity member requests or for serious constitutional violations, initiated and facilitated by Student Affairs.  
   6. Specific positional and other rights are subject to the entity’s internal guidelines.  
5. Faculty Advisors  
   1. A Society or Club may optionally include Professors/POD/Instructors as advisors/mentors at the Core Committee's discretion.  
6. Coordinators  
   1. Responsible for managing specific departments within the entity, ensuring smooth operations.  
   2. Appointed by the Secretary with consideration of other members' opinions.  
   3. Removal from position follows entity internal guidelines.  
7. Core Committee Responsibilities  
   1. Ensure adherence to this chapter of the Constitution.  
   2. Ensure members follow the general code and maintain Institute decorum.  
   3. Prevent dilution of the IITM brand.  
   4. Maintain well-defined internal regulations and administrative structure.  
   5. Maintain web presence and written rulebook including election/manuals and membership processes.  
   6. Maintain an official G-Space for active members.  
   7. Define criteria for membership screening and renewal.  
   8. Support auditing by submitting activity reports and plans each term to Student Government or Student Affairs for possible publication.  
   9. Submit exit reports including activity reports and future plans to Student Affairs each term to share with successor Core Committee members.  
   10. Make good-faith efforts to fulfill commitments to collaborators, guest speakers, members, and student body to avoid social criticism that may dilute the IITM brand.  
   11. Stick to their defined domain.  
   12. Avoid criticizing other entities and focus on collaboration to foster a productive environment.

## **SECTION VIII – ELECTIONS AND APPOINTMENTS** {#section-viii-–-elections-and-appointments}

1. Categories of Societies  
   1. Election-based Societies – Core Committee positions chosen by ballot of GB.  
   2. Nomination-based Societies – Core Committee positions proposed by outgoing Secretary.  
2. Eligibility Criteria  
   1. Secretary / Deputy Secretary (both categories):  
      1. CGPA ≥ 7.5;  
      2. completion of ≥ 32 academic credits;  
      3. prior full-term PoR;  
      4. no academic or non-academic misconduct conviction.  
   2. Co-ordinator:  
      1. CGPA ≥ 7.5;  
      2. no misconduct conviction.  
3. Election-based Process  
   1. General Body (active members) form the Electoral College.  
   2. List of Active Members finalized and published on Election Portal before polling.  
   3. Voting is online, secure, time-bound, supervised by the Election Commission.  
4. Nomination-based Process  
   1. Outgoing Secretary submits written nomination dossier with :  
      1. justification for nomination;  
      2. names and consent of nominees.  
   2. Nominees displayed on Election Portal under “Unopposed Nominations”.

## **SECTION IX – MEETINGS** {#section-ix-–-meetings}

1. Frequency and Quorum  
   1. The Core Committee meets at least once per month; quorum is half of CC membership.  
   2. The General Body meets at least once per term; quorum is 10% of Active Members or 20 members, whichever is lower.

## **SECTION X – CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINE** {#section-x-–-conduct-and-discipline}

1. Removal from Position  
   1. A PoR may be removed for misconduct, dereliction or ineligibility by two-thirds (⅔) vote of the Core Committee, subject to ratification by Student Affairs.

## **SECTION XI – REPORTING AND RECORDS** {#section-xi-–-reporting-and-records}

1. Term and Annual Reports  
   1. Each Society shall submit :  
      1. a Term Activity Report, approved by the respective Event Department Committee submitted to Student Affairs;  
      2. an Annual Report, approved by the respective Event Department Committee submitted to Student Affairs.

## **SECTION XII – LOGO, BRANDING AND ENDORSEMENT** {#section-xii-–-logo,-branding-and-endorsement}

1. Use of Names and Logos  
   1. Societies may adopt their own logos.  
   2. The name “IIT Madras” or any Institute emblem may be used only with prior written approval of the IIT Madras BS Degree Team.

## **SECTION XIII – MISCELLANEOUS** {#section-xiii-–-miscellaneous}

1. Commercial Activity  
   1. No Society shall conduct commercial ventures without explicit approval from Student Affairs.  
2. Standard Disclaimer  
   1. All Society communications shall carry the statement:  
      “Views expressed and activities conducted by this Society are solely those of its members and are not endorsed by IIT Madras BS.”

## **SECTION XIV – AMENDMENT, SUPREMACY AND COMMENCEMENT** {#section-xiv-–-amendment,-supremacy-and-commencement}

1. Amendment  
   1. This chapter may be amended by a two-thirds (⅔) vote of the societies and approval of Student Affairs.  
2. Supremacy  
   1. Institute statutes, policies and directives of Student Affairs shall prevail over any conflicting provision herein.

## **SECTION XV – DOMAINS AND DOMAIN SECRETARIES** {#section-xv-–-domains-and-domain-secretaries}

1. Domain Classification  
   1. Societies are grouped into the Domains : Technical, Sports and Cultural.  
   2. Student Affairs may create or dissolve a Domain upon due justification.  
2. Domain Secretaries  
   1. One (1) Event Department Secretary per Domain is a member of the SEC, as per the constitution.  
   2. Eligibility is solely by nomination of Student Affairs.
